identity.fantasy: A crossbow gunner who fires Darkslayer while moving, floods packs with extra bolts, and controls space with traps.
identity.one_line: A crossbow gunner who fires Darkslayer while moving, floods packs with extra bolts, and controls space with traps. The defining decision is contextual: Pack size and tank pacing decide whether Twilight Frenzy can function.

mechanics.core_loop: A crossbow specialist that casts Darkslayer while moving, generates extra bolts and Rage, and alternates Witchbane, Heartseeking Bolt, and Twilight Frenzy. A recent AoE guide reports easy, highly mobile dungeon damage and strong trap control, but weak survivability and dependence on sufficiently large pulls.
mechanics.single_target: Maintain the Heartseeking Bolt buff, use Tormentor, enter Rage, then fire six Witchbanes according to the captured guide. Darkslayer can be cast while moving, preserving uptime.
mechanics.aoe: At roughly three to four targets, use Twilight Frenzy with Darkslayer/Heartseeking Bolt, Tormentor, Rage cooldowns, and traps. The guide says small pulls starve the engine and tank pacing strongly affects results.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Cast-while-moving attacks are a defining strength and make repositioning unusually forgiving.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Its structural defensive package includes Heartseeking Bolt, Kingdom Hearts, Damnation, Daring Escape, Twilight Frenzy.
mechanics.group_utility: Group or control tools include Kingdom Hearts, Neverending Pursuit, Slayer, Tormenting the Tormented.

failure_modes.text: Using Twilight Frenzy on too few targets, missing Heartseeking upkeep, or taking avoidable damage punishes a spec the guide calls weak defensively.
Entering Rage before Heartseeking and Tormentor are ready shortens the useful six-Witchbane window.
Depending on Twilight Frenzy while the tank makes small pulls leaves the spec without the target count its AoE engine expects.
